description:

deletes the saved filter only — no customer, event or enrollment is touched.

description:
deleteCalendarPost removes one of the caller org's posts and answers 204. A
post already published is deleted from the calendar only — nothing is
retracted from the network it went out on.

id.description: ID is the post id from the path, as returned by create.

description:
deleteCampaign removes one of the caller org's campaigns and answers 204. A
campaign belonging to another org reads as not found and is left untouched.

id.description: ID is the campaign id from the path, as returned by create.

description:
removeSuppression re-subscribes an address on one channel and answers 204. An
address that is not on the list reads as not found.

address.description:
Address is the recipient, normalized (lower-cased, trimmed) so an opt-out
cannot be slipped past on a case or whitespace difference. Required.

channel.description:
Channel is the surface opted out of: email, sms, social, meta, google or
tiktok. Empty means email. Opting out of one leaves the others reachable.

reason.description:
Reason is a free-text note, capped at 1024 bytes. The public one-click

name: delete_v1_marketing_suppressions

would run — and reports how big it is and how many real mailboxes it reaches.
It is the honest answer to "is this send worth making": a cohort of 500 that
mails 3 says so, in deliverable and unmatched. Nothing is sent.

id.description: ID is the audience id from the path, as returned by create.

name: get_v1_marketing_audiences_id_preview

description:
listCalendarPosts returns the org's calendar, soonest scheduled first,
optionally narrowed to one status.

failed, canceled). Empty means every post.

getCalendarPost returns one of the caller org's posts, including the exact

id.description: ID is the post id from the path, as returned by create.

listCampaigns returns the org's campaigns, most recently updated first,
optionally narrowed to one lifecycle status.

status.description:
Status keeps only campaigns in that lifecycle state (draft, scheduled,
active, paused, completed). Empty means every campaign.

name: get_v1_marketing_campaigns

description:
getCampaign returns one of the caller org's campaigns. A campaign belonging to
another org reads as not found.

id.description: ID is the campaign id from the path, as returned by create.

name: get_v1_marketing_campaigns_id

description:
listPromos returns every promo the deployment offers with its live counters:
how many orgs have redeemed it and how many redemptions remain under the cap.
The promos are fleet-wide, not per-org — only the counters move.
name: get_v1_marketing_promos

description:
quotePromo prices a promo against a plan and seat count. It is PURE: nothing
is redeemed, credited or counted, so it is safe to call from a pricing page on
every keystroke. An inactive promo or an exhausted cap quotes ineligible with
the reason rather than erroring.

code.description: Code is the promo code from the path.

plan.description:
Plan is the plan being priced: pro, max or team. Anything else (including
the free Developer plan) has no list price and so nothing to discount.

seats.description:
Seats is the Team seat count; 0 means 1, and it is ignored for the
single-seat plans.

name: get_v1_marketing_promos_code_eligibility

description:
getRedemption returns the caller org's OWN redemption of a promo — an
org-scoped read, so it can never surface another tenant's. Not found when this
org has not redeemed it.

code.description: Code is the promo code from the path, e.g. "first1000".

name: get_v1_marketing_promos_code_redemption

description: listSequences returns the org's drip sequences, most recently updated first.

limit.description: Limit caps the rows returned; 0 means 200 and nothing above 1000 is honoured.

name: get_v1_marketing_sequences

description:
getSequence returns one of the caller org's sequences together with its steps
in send order. A sequence belonging to another org reads as not found.

id.description: ID is the sequence id from the path, as returned by create.

name: get_v1_marketing_sequences_id

description:
listEnrollments returns who is walking one sequence, most recently enrolled
first, with each walk's current step and next due time.

id.description: ID is the sequence id from the path.

limit.description: Limit caps the rows returned; 0 means 200 and nothing above 1000 is honoured.

name: get_v1_marketing_sequences_id_enrollments

description: listSteps returns one sequence's steps in send order.

id.description: ID is the sequence id from the path, as returned by create.

name: get_v1_marketing_sequences_id_steps

description:
summary rolls up the caller org's campaigns: how many there are, how many are
active, and the summed budget and spend in cents.
name: get_v1_marketing_summary

description:
listSuppressions returns the org's opt-out list, newest first — everyone the
send gate will refuse to deliver to.

limit.description: Limit caps the rows returned; 0 means 200 and nothing above 1000 is honoured.

name: get_v1_marketing_suppressions

description:
unsubscribe is the PUBLIC one-click endpoint (no principal): a recipient
clicks the signed link in an email footer. The token binds (org, channel,
address), so a caller can only opt OUT exactly the tuple it was minted for —
never another address and never another org. An invalid token is refused, and
a deployment with no KMS-sealed key refuses rather than accepting anything.

address.description: Address is the recipient to opt out.

channel.description: Channel is the surface to opt out of.

org.description: Org is the org the link was minted for.

token.description:
Token is the HMAC over (org, channel, address). It is the ONLY authority
here — there is no principal — so it binds the request to one tuple and
nothing else.

name: get_v1_marketing_unsubscribe

description:
createAudience saves a cohort filter for the caller's org. Name is required.
Omitting event saves the WHOLE-ORG audience — every mailable customer — which
needs no analytics warehouse; naming one narrows that roster to the customers
who fired it within windowDays.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt and UpdatedAt are unix seconds, both server-assigned.

event.description:
Event is the analytics event a member must have fired. EMPTY MEANS NO
FILTER: the audience is then every mailable customer in the org, and no
warehouse is consulted.

id.description: ID is the server-assigned audience id ("aud_" + 128 random bits).

name.description: Name is the audience's label. Required, trimmed, capped at 1024 bytes.

windowDays.description:
WindowDays is how far back the event counts, ending now. 0 means 30 and
nothing above 3650 is honoured. Ignored when Event is empty.

name: post_v1_marketing_audiences

description:
createCalendarPost adds a post to the content calendar. Channel and body are
required. A scheduledAt in the future makes the post "scheduled" and the
durable sweep publishes it when it comes due — claimed once, so a post
publishes at most once; without one it stays a draft.

body.description: Body is the post text. Required.

channel.description:
Channel is the target network: x, facebook, instagram, linkedin, tiktok,
youtube or threads. Required — a post must name where it goes.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt and UpdatedAt are unix seconds, both server-assigned.

error.description:
Error is the exact reason the last publish attempt failed — the honest
record behind a "failed" status, never a faked success.

id.description: ID is the server-assigned post id ("cal_" + 128 random bits).

publishedAt.description: PublishedAt is when the publish succeeded; 0 until it does.

scheduledAt.description:
ScheduledAt is the unix publish time; 0 leaves the post a draft, and any
value makes it "scheduled" for the durable sweep to pick up.

status.description: Status is draft, scheduled, published, failed or canceled. Server-owned.

title.description: Title is the post's internal label, capped at 1024 bytes.

name: post_v1_marketing_calendar

description:
publishCalendarPost publishes a post NOW, synchronously, whatever its
schedule. No social connector is wired today, so every channel answers an
honest 501 naming the seam a real one would plug into, and the post is
recorded failed with that exact reason — never a faked "published".

id.description: ID is the post id from the path, as returned by create.

name: post_v1_marketing_calendar_id_publish

description:
createCampaign registers a campaign in the caller's org. Name is required;
channel defaults to email and status to draft, and a future scheduledAt with
no explicit status makes the campaign "scheduled". Budget and spend are cents
and are clamped to >= 0. The id, createdAt and updatedAt of the input are
ignored — the server assigns them.

budget.description: Budget and Spend are minor units (USD cents), clamped to >= 0.

channel.description:
Channel is the delivery surface: email, sms, social, meta, google or
tiktok. Empty means email.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt and UpdatedAt are unix seconds, both server-assigned.

id.description: ID is the server-assigned campaign id ("camp_" + 128 random bits).

name.description: Name is the campaign's label. Required, trimmed, capped at 1024 bytes.

objective.description: Objective is the free-text goal ("signups"), capped at 1024 bytes.

scheduledAt.description:
ScheduledAt is the unix send time; 0 means unscheduled. Setting it on a
campaign with no explicit status makes that status "scheduled".

status.description:
Status is the lifecycle: draft, scheduled, active, paused or completed.
Empty means draft.

name: post_v1_marketing_campaigns

description:
scheduleCampaign sets a campaign's send time and moves it to "scheduled". A
scheduledAt of 0 clears the schedule and returns it to "draft".

id.description: ID is the campaign id from the path.

scheduledAt.description: ScheduledAt is the unix send time. 0 clears the schedule.

name: post_v1_marketing_campaigns_id_schedule

description:
redeemPromo redeems the promo for the caller's org, crediting the discount
value to its wallet through the finance ledger. Three guards run under one
lock so the cap cannot be raced past: the fleet-wide redemption cap, one
redemption per org, and one per payment instrument.

It is IDEMPOTENT: an org that already redeemed gets its original redemption
back with alreadyRedeemed true and is not credited twice.

code.description: Code is the promo code from the path.

instrument.description:
Instrument identifies the payment method. It is the anti-farming key: one
redemption per instrument, fleet-wide.

plan.description: Plan is the plan being redeemed against: pro, max or team.

seats.description:
Seats is the Team seat count; 0 means 1. Seats beyond the promo's
teamSeatCap bill at list.

name: post_v1_marketing_promos_code_redeem

description:
createSequence registers a drip sequence in the caller's org. Name is
required; status defaults to draft, and a sequence must be ACTIVE before it
will accept enrollments. The id, createdAt and updatedAt of the input are
ignored — the server assigns them.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt and UpdatedAt are unix seconds, both server-assigned.

id.description: ID is the server-assigned sequence id ("seq_" + 128 random bits).

name.description: Name is the sequence's label. Required, trimmed, capped at 1024 bytes.

status.description:
Status is the lifecycle: draft, active or archived. Empty means draft, and
ONLY an active sequence accepts enrollments.

name: post_v1_marketing_sequences

description:
enroll adds one contact or a whole audience to a sequence and schedules the
first step for each. The sequence must be ACTIVE (a draft sends nothing), and
the request must name exactly one of address or audienceId.

Enrolling is ALL this does: the message itself is sent later by the drip
engine, through the suppression gate, so an opted-out customer can be enrolled
here and still never be mailed. Re-posting is safe — an address this sequence
already took is counted in alreadyEnrolled and never double-dripped — which is
what makes retrying a partially-applied announcement a resume rather than a
second send.

address.description:
Address is a single recipient, normalized (lower-cased, trimmed) before
use. Give this OR audienceId, never both and never neither.

audienceId.description:
AudienceID fans the sequence out over a saved audience, resolved live to
the org's mailable customers. Email only.

channel.description:
Channel is the delivery surface; empty means email. An audience resolves
mailboxes, so an audience enroll must be email.

id.description: ID is the sequence id from the path.

name: post_v1_marketing_sequences_id_enroll

description:
cancelEnrollment stops one walk mid-sequence and answers 204: no further step
is sent, and steps already delivered are not recalled. Only an ACTIVE
enrollment can be canceled — one already completed or canceled reads as not
found.

eid.description:
EID is the enrollment id from the path, as returned by a single-address
enroll.

id.description: ID is the sequence id from the path.

name: post_v1_marketing_sequences_id_enrollments_eid_cancel

description:
setSequenceStatus flips draft/active/archived — the activation gate for
sending, since only an active sequence accepts enrollments. It does not touch
enrollments already walking: archiving stops new ones, not in-flight ones.

id.description: ID is the sequence id from the path.

status.description:
Status is draft, active or archived. Required; there is no default here,
unlike on create. Only an active sequence accepts enrollments.

name: post_v1_marketing_sequences_id_status

description:
addStep appends a message to the END of a sequence: the new step's idx is one
past the last, so steps arrive in the order they are added. Body is required
and delaySeconds must be >= 0. Adding a step does not disturb enrollments
already walking — one that has passed this index simply never sees it.

body.description: Body is the message text. Required.

delaySeconds.description:
DelaySeconds is how long after the previous step this one sends (after
enrollment, for the first step). Must be >= 0.

id.description: SequenceID is the sequence id from the path (the route's :id).

subject.description: Subject is the email subject line, capped at 1024 bytes.

name: post_v1_marketing_sequences_id_steps

description:
addSuppression records an opt-out for the org (admin / self-service
management). Address is required; channel defaults to email. It is idempotent:
re-suppressing the same tuple keeps the original record rather than erroring.
From here on the ONE send gate refuses that recipient on that channel.

address.description:
Address is the recipient, normalized (lower-cased, trimmed) so an opt-out
cannot be slipped past on a case or whitespace difference. Required.

channel.description:
Channel is the surface opted out of: email, sms, social, meta, google or
tiktok. Empty means email. Opting out of one leaves the others reachable.

reason.description:
Reason is a free-text note, capped at 1024 bytes. The public one-click
endpoint records "one-click unsubscribe".

name: post_v1_marketing_suppressions

description:
updateCalendarPost replaces a post's editable fields. It is a full write, not
a patch, and it RESETS the lifecycle from the schedule: a scheduledAt makes
the post "scheduled" again and none makes it a draft — so editing a failed
post requeues it rather than leaving it stuck.

body.description: Body is the post text. Required.

channel.description:
Channel is the target network: x, facebook, instagram, linkedin, tiktok,
youtube or threads. Required — a post must name where it goes.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt and UpdatedAt are unix seconds, both server-assigned.

error.description:
Error is the exact reason the last publish attempt failed — the honest
record behind a "failed" status, never a faked success.

id.description: ID is the server-assigned post id ("cal_" + 128 random bits).

publishedAt.description: PublishedAt is when the publish succeeded; 0 until it does.

scheduledAt.description:
ScheduledAt is the unix publish time; 0 leaves the post a draft, and any
value makes it "scheduled" for the durable sweep to pick up.

status.description: Status is draft, scheduled, published, failed or canceled. Server-owned.

title.description: Title is the post's internal label, capped at 1024 bytes.

name: put_v1_marketing_calendar_id

description:
updateCampaign replaces a campaign's editable fields. It is a full write, not
a patch: every field takes the value in the body, and an omitted one is
cleared. The id comes from the path — the body cannot retarget another
campaign — and createdAt is never rewritten.

budget.description: Budget and Spend are minor units (USD cents), clamped to >= 0.

channel.description:
Channel is the delivery surface: email, sms, social, meta, google or
tiktok. Empty means email.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt and UpdatedAt are unix seconds, both server-assigned.

id.description: ID is the server-assigned campaign id ("camp_" + 128 random bits).

name.description: Name is the campaign's label. Required, trimmed, capped at 1024 bytes.

objective.description: Objective is the free-text goal ("signups"), capped at 1024 bytes.

scheduledAt.description:
ScheduledAt is the unix send time; 0 means unscheduled. Setting it on a
campaign with no explicit status makes that status "scheduled".

status.description:
Status is the lifecycle: draft, scheduled, active, paused or completed.
Empty means draft.

name: put_v1_marketing_campaigns_id
